name: Paraguay
snapshot: Pedro Alliana became president on 6 November 2026 after the Senate removed Santiago Peña 44 to 1 over the collapse of Ueno Bank, in which Peña had held shares.
culture: Paraguay is the only country in the Americas where most people speak an Indigenous language, Guaraní, which is official alongside Spanish. Tereré, cold yerba mate, is drunk everywhere. The harp and the polka paraguaya are central to its music. The Jesuit missions of the 17th and 18th centuries left UNESCO-listed ruins.
society: Paraguay is a top exporter of soy and beef, and the Itaipú and Yacyretá dams produce more electricity than it uses. Land is very unequally distributed. It is one of the few countries still recognising Taiwan instead of China. Smuggling and money laundering in the tri-border area with Brazil and Argentina are a concern.
situation: Santiago Peña, elected in 2023 with the backing of former president Horacio Cartes, fell over the collapse of Ueno Bank, a digital lender with about three million customers owned by his former business partners, which the central bank seized on 3 November 2026. After Cartes and the Colorado Party turned on him, deputies impeached him 78 to 0 and on 6 November the Senate removed him 44 to 1. Vice President Pedro Alliana, also a Colorado and himself under investigation, was sworn in to serve until August 2028, with Senator Antonio Barrios as vice president. On 7 November a judge ordered Peña held in pretrial detention on charges of aggravated breach of trust.
power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for a single five-year term; Congress has a Senate and a Chamber of Deputies, both dominated by the Colorado Party.

Corruption and the Colorado party's grip

story: Jesuit missions and the Guaraní language shaped Paraguay. In the War of the Triple Alliance from 1864 to 1870 against Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay, it lost perhaps half its population. General Alfredo Stroessner ruled from 1954 to 1989, and his Colorado Party has governed almost continuously since 1947.
